tiles.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Calef and Parker (2016), USGS Astrogeology

overlays.label: Slope limits
overlays.description: Amber: 15 to 20 deg (caution penalty). Red: above 20 deg (impassable). Slope of 3 m cells from the 1 m DEM. Cell size and penalty are assumptions.
overlays.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Parker and Calef (2016), USGS Astrogeology

overlays.label: Boulder shadows
overlays.description: Compact dark blobs in the orthophoto, kept as boulder shadows. Long thin shadows (ridges) are rejected. Detection floor about 1.5 m. Thresholds are assumptions.
overlays.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Calef and Parker (2016), USGS Astrogeology

overlays.label: THEMIS day IR
overlays.description: Daytime infrared brightness (about 163 m pixels). Image brightness, not calibrated temperature. Display only.

overlays.label: CRISM SINDEX2 (sulfate)
overlays.description: Sulfate index from frt000058a3_07_su165j_mtr3.img (about 18 m pixels), stretched min to max in the AOI.

overlays.label: Science value
overlays.description: Weighted sum of the normalized CRISM sulfate index and the boxwork ridge score. Weights are assumptions.
overlays.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/JHU-APL; NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Parker and Calef (2016), USGS Astrogeology

overlays.label: Terrain sky cover
overlays.description: Where terrain blocks part of the sky (zenith-weighted). Partial shielding only: only the habitat and the rover are full shelters.
overlays.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Parker and Calef (2016), USGS Astrogeology

overlays.label: Low-confidence DEM
overlays.description: Cells where a measured test finds stripes that follow the DEM pixel columns (a mosaic artifact, not terrain). Threshold is an assumption.
overlays.source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Parker and Calef (2016), USGS Astrogeology

habitat.source: pipeline rule (ASSUMPTION): most interior cell of the flat zone (slope < 5 deg, area >= 2500 m2) nearest the AOI center

shelters.source: pipeline rule (ASSUMPTION): rover parked at the pickup zone nearest the middle of the science stops

sources.label: Elevation (1 m DEM)
sources.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Parker and Calef (2016), USGS Astrogeology

sources.label: Orthophoto basemap
sources.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/UArizona; Calef and Parker (2016), USGS Astrogeology

notes.text: DEM quality: the east 100 m of the area showed stripe and seam signs in a Phase 0 check. A measured test (stripes that follow the DEM pixel columns) marks 18% of that strip and 1.4% of the rest of the area as low confidence. Slopes there can be wrong. The test threshold is an assumption.
The USGS DEM uses CTX or HRSC elevation where HiRISE stereo is missing. Those parts are smoother, so small steep features can be missing.
Boulders smaller than about 1.5 m cannot be seen in HiRISE images. The boulder layer misses them.
THEMIS layer: image brightness at about 163 m per pixel, not calibrated temperature. Display only.
CRISM sulfate index (SINDEX2) has about 18 m pixels: one value covers many routing cells.
Terrain sky cover counts the sky beyond the edge of the area as open. Terrain gives partial shielding only.
Part of the west edge of the orthophoto is grayscale: HiRISE color is missing there. It is not an error.
Rover pickup zones are flat areas the crew can walk to. Rover driving access to them is not modeled (assumption).

MARS_GRAVITY.source: NASA Mars Fact Sheet, mean surface gravity (updated 2025). Was 3.71 (2007 edition) (changed 2026-11-14)

ONE_WAY_LIGHT_TIME_MIN.source: Light time over the Earth-Mars distance, 54.6 to 401 million km. Was 4 to 24 (changed 2026-11-14)

ROUTING_CELL_SIZE_M.source: HiRISE DTM effective resolution is about 3x its 1 m post spacing; 1 m slopes are noise

MAX_WALK_RADIUS_M.source: NASA EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B (2020), p. 38: traverses up to 2 km away from the lander

MAX_SLOPE_DEG.source: NASA EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B (2020), p. 38: walking up/down/across a slope of up to 20 deg

CAUTION_SLOPE_DEG.source: Pena-Asensio et al. 2023, Acta Astronautica (automated Artemis traverses): slopes limited to 15 deg. Not a NASA limit

RESCUE_DISTANCE_M.source: NASA Lunar Rescue System webinar (NTRS 20250000528, 2025): one crewmember transports an incapacitated crewmember up to 2 km, slopes up to 20 deg

EVA_DURATION_H.source: NASA EVA-EXP-0042 Rev B (2020), p. 29: EVAs between 4 and 8 hours (6 +/- 2). Adjustable.

AVG_METABOLIC_KJ_PER_H.source: Apollo PLSS design average, 1200 BTU/h (NASA technical report, NTRS 19720019467). Was 1688 = 1600 BTU/h, a press value (changed 2026-11-14)

STOP_DWELL_MIN.source: Apollo 12, second EVA: seven major stops, "On average, they had about twenty minutes at each location" (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, docs/research.md, section 2.3). One traverse, not a rule. Adjustable. (project owner, 2026-11-14)

STATION_WORK_W.source: Apollo geological station activity, 244 kcal/h = 284 W (Moore, NTRS 19910001262, p. 2, citing Waligora and Horrigan 1975)

RESERVE_FRACTION.source: Safety margin kept unused on return. Adjustable.

BUDDY_LAG_S.source: Default time crewmember B walks behind A on the same path (simulate delaysS.B, the app's buddy slider starts here). No published value. Adjustable in the app. (project owner, 2026-11-15)

CAUTION_SLOPE_PENALTY.source: Extra cost multiplier for 15-20 deg cells

SUIT_AND_GEAR_MASS_KG.source: Suit + life support + tools. No Mars suit exists yet. Adjustable. NASA designs its lunar rescue device for up to 342 kg (755 lb) crew + suit; the project owner kept 80 + 120 = 200 kg (2026-11-14)

WALK_SPEED_M_PER_S.source: Norcross et al., NASA/TP-2010-216115, p. 56: site-to-site walking 1.1 to 1.4 m/s (lunar). Lower end chosen. Was 0.9, no source found (changed 2026-11-14)

RESCUE_SPEED_M_PER_S.source: Slower pace while carrying a crewmember. Adjustable.

SANTEE_LEVEL_MASS_COEF.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_level mass coefficient (W/kg), via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_LEVEL_OFFSET_W.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_level offset (W), via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_LEVEL_SPEED_COEF.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_level speed coefficient (s/m), via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_LEVEL_BASE.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_level constant term, via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_UPHILL_COEF.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_up coefficient, via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_DOWNHILL_COEF.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_down coefficient, via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_DOWNHILL_DECAY_BASE.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_down decay base, via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_DOWNHILL_DECAY_DEG.source: Santee et al. 2001, W_down decay angle (deg), via Johnson et al. 2010, Table 2

SANTEE_MIN_LEVEL_FRACTION.source: Floor W_total >= W_level * 0.5. Not in the source: it stops steep downhill edges from giving near-zero cost

METABOLIC_MODEL_AT_MARS_GRAVITY.value: Santee et al. 2001 with g = MARS_GRAVITY
METABOLIC_MODEL_AT_MARS_GRAVITY.source: The model was fitted on Earth (treadmill, about 1.34 m/s). Limited validation at reduced gravity (docs/research.md, section 2.5)

SEP_MAY2024_TOTAL_UGY.source: NASA release, June 2024: about 8,100 micrograys beside Curiosity for the 20 May 2024 event (a total, not a rate)

SEP_ARRIVAL.source: NASA release, June 2024: the charged particles reached Mars in tens of minutes

SEP_SHELTER_TARGET_MIN.source: Warn when the crew needs longer than this to reach a full shelter. 30 min = the lower end of the 30 to 60 min particle onset after the 2013-2014 flares (docs/research.md, section 2.6). SEP_ARRIVAL gives no exact number. Adjustable. (project owner, 2026-11-14)

TERRAIN_SHIELD_MODEL.source: Low-angle particles cross more atmosphere, so overhead sky matters most

SHIELD_PARTIAL_MAX_SKY.source: A cell counts as a terrain partial shelter when its open-sky share (shield.bin / 255) is at or below this. On the real site the walkable cells run from 0.906 (1st percentile) to 1.0; 0.90 keeps 4,945 cells (0.65%), the most sheltered ones under ridges and walls. Gives no dose reduction number. (project owner, 2026-11-15)

ROUGHNESS_DETREND_SIGMA_M.source: Gaussian sigma removed from the 1 m DEM before roughness is measured, so the cell slope does not count as roughness

ROUGHNESS_COST_PER_M.source: Multiplier = 1 + this * roughness RMS (m). AOI median RMS is about 0.15 m, so the median cell costs about 7% more than smooth ground. No published Mars value. Adjustable.

BOULDER_COST_FACTOR.source: Extra cost for a cell with a detected boulder shadow (walk around or over blocks). Adjustable.

BOULDER_LOCAL_WINDOW_M.source: Window for the local mean brightness, so dark sand does not count as shadow

BOULDER_SHADOW_DARKNESS.source: Shadow pixel = darker than 0.6 x local mean. Checked by eye on two 200 m crops.

BOULDER_MIN_SHADOW_AREA_M2.source: 4 pixels. Matches the ~1.5 m detection floor (see Data limits)

BOULDER_MAX_SHADOW_AREA_M2.source: Larger dark blobs are outcrop or scarp shadows

BOULDER_MAX_ELONGATION.source: Ratio of principal axes. Build plan: keep compact roundish blobs, reject long thin ridge shadows

SHIELD_AZIMUTHS.source: Directions used to find the horizon

SHIELD_SEARCH_RADIUS_M.source: Horizon search distance. Terrain outside the AOI counts as open sky. Open sky share per direction = cos^2(horizon angle) (TERRAIN_SHIELD_MODEL).

DEM_QUALITY_COLUMN_RUN_M.source: Run length down a column. Real ridges drift off a pixel column within this distance

DEM_QUALITY_WINDOW_M.source: Averaging window of the coherence score

DEM_QUALITY_COHERENCE_MIN.source: Threshold, just below the artifact median (0.46)

DEM_QUALITY_MIN_AREA_M2.source: 200 cells. Smaller flagged patches are dropped as noise

SCIENCE_WEIGHT_SULFATE.source: Weight of normalized CRISM SINDEX2 (band 42 of the summary-parameter product, read from the label)

SCIENCE_WEIGHT_RIDGE.source: Weight of the boxwork ridge score

RIDGE_RADIUS_M.source: Ridge score = height above the mean of the cells within this radius (0 if below)

SCIENCE_NORMALIZE_LOW_PERCENTILE.source: Each part is stretched 0..1 between these AOI percentiles

SCIENCE_NORMALIZE_HIGH_PERCENTILE.source: Same. Was 98: the top stops then all scored 255 and could not be ranked (project owner chose 99.5 on 2026-11-14)

SCIENCE_STOP_COUNT.source: Maximum stops in meta.json waypoints. Stops are real Curiosity stops (sols aoi_sol_min to aoi_sol_max), highest science value first. With the spacing below, 7 fit on the 2025 track

SCIENCE_STOP_MIN_SPACING_M.source: Minimum distance between candidate stops, and from the habitat

ROVER_PICKUP_MAX_SLOPE_DEG.source: Flat cell for a rover pickup (Data limits, "Contingency recovery"). Also used for the habitat site

ROVER_PICKUP_MIN_AREA_M2.source: Flat zone must be at least 30 m x 30 m

ROVER_PICKUP_MIN_SPACING_M.source: Spread the zones over the area

HABITAT_MIN_FLAT_AREA_M2.source: Habitat = most interior cell of the flat zone (>= 50 m x 50 m) nearest the AOI center. The site YAML can override it (habitat_lat, habitat_lon)

TILE_JPEG_QUALITY.source: JPEG quality of the basemap tiles: a balance of file size (offline cache) and detail. Display only

DEM_EAST_STRIP_M.source: Width of the east strip where the Phase 0 check saw stripe and seam signs (columns about 2900 to 3000, docs/datasets.md, section 1). Used only to report the DEM quality test result in meta.json `notes`

EVA_ENERGY_BUDGET_J.source: Walk-back budget. Using the design average rate as a whole-EVA energy budget is our choice. Adjustable with setParams.

NO_CORNER_CUTTING.source: A diagonal move is allowed only when both side neighbours are passable, so a route cannot slip diagonally through an impassable band

TURN_BACK_MODEL.value: remaining energy spent at STATION_WORK_W while the crew stays at `position`

TURN_ANGLE_DEG.source: A heading change above this starts a new turn-by-turn instruction (docs/data-contract.md, section 4.2). Smaller changes follow the terrain without a new step. (project owner, 2026-11-15)

SCIENCE_PEAK_COUNT.source: Science planner: at most this many science-value peaks (local maxima of science_val.bin) join the Curiosity stops as candidates, at least SCIENCE_STOP_MIN_SPACING_M apart (docs/data-contract.md, section 4.1). Peaks have no Curiosity image. (project owner, 2026-11-15)

SCIENCE_VALUE_MAX.source: Top of the science value scale: science_val.bin and waypoint scienceValue are uint8 0 to 255 (docs/data-contract.md, section 1) (added 2026-11-15)

TIMELINE_STEP_S.source: EVA time slider step: one minute. Display choice

OVERLAY_OPACITY.source: Opacity of the meta.json overlays, so the basemap stays visible below. Display choice

MAP_MIN_ZOOM.source: Leaflet zoom z draws 2^z pixels per meter: -3 shows the 3 km site in about 375 px. Display choice

MAP_MAX_ZOOM.source: 16 px per meter, past the 0.5 m orthophoto pixels. Display choice

PAN_MARGIN_FRACTION.source: Share of the site size the user may pan past the edge. Display choice
